title: The Annuity Trap That Never Went Away — Surrender Fee Traps (Reel)
description: Not one lawsuit — a decade-long documented pattern. Over $130M in real settlements against annuity insurers for surrender-charge practices, plus what California law requires insurers to disclose on the cover page, right now.
sourceCitation: Vaccarino v. Midland National Life Insurance Co., No. 2:11-cv-05858, C.D. Cal. ($31M settlement). In re Midland National Life Insurance Co. Annuity Sales Practices Litigation, D. Iowa ($80M settlement, final approval 2012, 70,000+ seniors). National Western Life Insurance Co. ($21M RICO settlement). California Insurance Code § 10127.13. This video uses AI-generated narration. Educational content only, not financial or legal advice.

scenes.narrationText: In 2025, someone wrote this online: "The stock market had returns of twenty-five percent each year. I received about one and a half to two and a half percent — and the surrender fees to get out are horrendous." This isn't a new complaint. It's the same one people have been making for over a decade.

These are real settlements. Thirty-one million dollars from Midland National, over deferred annuities the lawsuit alleged were marketed with false bonus promises. Eighty million dollars, benefiting more than seventy thousand seniors, in a separate Midland case alleging the company sold annuities that wouldn't mature until after buyers' life expectancy. Twenty-one million from National Western, in a case alleging annuities were aggressively marketed to elderly clients with, quote, "huge surrender penalties." These cases are years old. The product design that caused them hasn't gone away.

Here's what's actually true, right now, if you're in California: state law requires every annuity contract to disclose its surrender charge, in bold twelve-point print, on the cover page or policy jacket. Not buried in page forty. On the cover.
If you already own an annuity, find that disclosure box. Know your exact surrender percentage and exactly when it ends.

visual.text:
Find the surrender charge box on your policy's cover page or first page.

Ask your agent, in writing: "What is my surrender charge today, and when does it reach zero?"
